definitions.gloss: to dawn; to grow light; to break (of day)
definitions.explanation: Describes the sky gradually becoming lighter as dawn approaches. A literary and evocative word that conveys the slow, whitening spread of light before sunrise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{東|ひがし}→東：02250_higashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{白々|しらじら}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{明|あ}けて→明ける：21288_akeru⟧きた。
examples.english: The eastern sky began to grow light.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{徹|てっ}して→徹する：12567_tessuru⟧⟦{話|はな}している→話す：00467_hanasu⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{白々|しらじら}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{明|あ}けた→明ける：21288_akeru⟧。
examples.english: While we talked through the night, the sky gradually grew light.

examples.japanese: {白々|しらじら}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{明|あ}ける→明ける：21288_akeru⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧、⟦{漁師|りょうし}→漁師：21205_ryoushi⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧すでに⟦{船|ふね}→船：00775_fune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}していた→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: Under the brightening dawn sky, the fishermen had already set out in their boats.

notes:
Composed of {白々|しらじら} (whitish, pale) and ⟦{明|あ}ける→明ける：21288_akeru⟧ (to open/dawn). A literary expression that paints the visual scene of the sky turning pale before sunrise. Often used in the pattern {白々|しらじら}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{明|あ}ける→明ける：21288_akeru⟧, where ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ marks the manner of the dawning.

USAGE:
This word belongs to literary and poetic registers. In everyday speech, {夜|よ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{明|あ}ける→明ける：21288_akeru⟧ (dawn breaks) or ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (it becomes morning) is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{白々|しらじら}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{明|あ}ける→明ける：21288_akeru⟧: the sky grows pale with dawn
- {白々|しらじら}⟦{明|あ}け→明け：13157_ake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧: the brightening dawn sky

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{夜明|よあ}け→夜明け：03655_yoake⟧: dawn/daybreak — the standard neutral term
- ⟦{明|あ}け{方|がた}→明け方：17595_akegata⟧: early dawn — refers to the time period
- {東雲|しののめ}: dawn (literary) — classical/poetic synonym
